entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - 1, Harippad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The above case is charge sheeted against the petitioner alleging offences punishable under Sections 420, 354, 511 and 376 r/w 34 of IPC.
2.

After hearing the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner in length, I am of the considered opinion that, without expressing anything on merit, the petitioner can be allowed to file a discharge petition before the trial court, at the appropriate stage.
If any observation is made by this Court in this order, that will affect the contentions of the petitioner in the discharge petition.

Therefore,
granting liberty to the petitioner to file a discharge petition, this Crl.MC can be disposed of.
But, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that, the petitioner has not appeared before the jurisdictional court.

If he surrender before the jurisdictional court within three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and file a bail application, the learned Magistrate will allow the bail application in order to committ the proceedings to the competent court.

After committal, the petitioner is free to file a discharge petition and if such a petition is filed, the jurisdictional court will consider the same and pass appropriate orders in it, in accordance with law.
With these observations, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is disposed of.
